A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPlus optimizer and support a reliable comparison of text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Appendices A.1-A.4 match across versions, and v3's additional tables and checklist are readable.

before.justification: V1 reports original optimizer comparisons on language modeling, image classification, and diffusion modeling, together with stability, scaling, and averaging experiments in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains those original experiments and adds quantitative eigendecomposition-frequency and cross-optimizer iterate-averaging comparisons in Tables 1-2.

M1.justification: SPlus retains historical eigenbases, instant-sign normalization, symmetric shape scaling, and iterate averaging. V3 corrects the left-eigenbasis transposes in Equations 11 and 15 and Algorithm 2 to match the JAX implementation already present in v1 Appendix A.1; the implementation itself is unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate OpenWebText language modeling and ImageNet classification and latent diffusion, using the same initialization, 10K, and 50K checkpoint scenarios. The additional ablations remain within the existing language-modeling coverage.

E2.justification: The Figure 6 comparator lineup is retained, but v3 Table 2 adds evaluated Adam-plus-iterate-averaging and SOAP-plus-iterate-averaging variants. V3 also changes the displayed Shampoo algorithm from inverse-square-root to inverse-fourth-root factors and says it additionally considers half-power Shampoo; the reported scores do not separately identify these variants or establish reruns.

E3.justification: V3 specifies Muon weight decay as 0.001, differing from v1's general 0.1 specification; unchanged scores do not establish that experiments were rerun. The added frequency analysis includes cache intervals of 1 and 250 beyond the earlier sweep and reports timing under a 1,000-step LLM-Init protocol. The main 10,000-step comparison design remains unchanged.

E4.justification: V3 substantially extends the existing cache-duration and averaging analyses. Table 1 quantifies the performance/runtime tradeoff, while Table 2 compares averaging across Adam, SOAP, and SPlus and includes memory requirements. The latter directly tests whether SPlus's advantage comes from its gradient transformation or from averaging, addressing an important alternative explanation absent from v1's controls.

E5.justification: V1 states that random seed and data order are controlled. V3 checklist item 7 additionally discloses one trial per optimizer, objective, checkpoint, and learning-rate configuration because of computational constraints. This is newly explicit run-count information, not evidence of changed replication; no error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: Figure 6 and the matched appendix results remain numerically unchanged. New Tables 1-2 add substantial timing and component-comparison findings: Table 1 reports SPlus time-to-Adam of 0.65 at cache interval 250, and Table 2 reports SOAP with averaging outperforming SPlus at LLM-10K (0.416 versus 0.422) and LLM-50K (0.317 versus 0.348). These are additional experimental findings, not improvements in retained results.

T1.justification: V3 revises the Shampoo/Kronecker formulas, including changing factor powers from -1/2 to -1/4 and replacing an exact factorization claim with an approximation. It adds half factors to quadratic penalties and corrects SPlus eigenbasis transposes. These are mathematical revisions, although Equations 8-9 still mix factor and inverse-factor definitions; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion change the headline claim from matching Adam within 44% of gradient steps and 62% of wall-clock time to ranges of 44-58% and 62-83%. The three central optimizer contributions and the cross-domain efficiency claim remain intact.

C2.justification: Section 5.1 newly connects averaging's benefits across optimizers to the constant learning-rate schedule and acknowledges that SOAP with averaging can outperform SPlus at greater memory cost. V3 also flags constant schedules as less standard for language modeling, qualifies Shampoo divergence to the tested setting, and describes wall-clock results as rough estimates.

D1.justification: V3 newly specifies the constant schedule after warmup and PSGD's Kron variant, and tabulates comparator memory requirements. It removes the practitioner section, including the Adam-to-SPlus learning-rate conversion, recommended 0.2 starting rate, and integration guidance. The repository access information and Appendix A.1 implementation remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds Morwani et al., A New Perspective on Shampoo's Preconditioner, in connection with half-power Shampoo. It refines the relationship to SOAP through the new averaging comparison and memory tradeoff. The broader related-work discussion and existing references are retained.

P1.justification: Most prose and section organization are retained, with localized revisions to mathematical explanations, evaluation, and limitations. The practitioner section is replaced by acknowledgments, a NeurIPS checklist is appended, and the first-page publication header changes.

P2.justification: V3 adds two main-text tables for frequency and averaging analyses. Existing plots and the Figure 6 comparison layout are retained; captions receive limited edits, appendix Tables 1-2 become Tables 3-4, and surrounding pagination adjusts.

improvement.justification: Tables 1-2 improve evidence about runtime costs and the contribution of averaging, including the useful finding that SOAP with averaging can outperform SPlus. Explicit disclosure of the constant schedule and single-trial design also improves transparency. These gains are limited by removed practitioner guidance, retained broad superiority language, and inconsistencies in the revised Shampoo equations; the original benchmark results remain unchanged.
